text:
Irene: heads-up: onboarding sampleapp failed at api call to list datasets. Curl works but Go SDK returns 400: "invalid filter".
Mark: can you paste curl + sdk snippet?
Irene: curl that works:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/datasets?filter=name:eq:training" 
```
Irene: Go SDK (failing):
```go
client.Admin.ListDatasets(context.Background(), client.WithFilter("name=eq:training"))
// -> 400 invalid filter: unexpected operator
```
Luis: looks like the SDK is translating operators differently. The REST expects colon-separated operator syntax `field:op:value` but Go helper converted `:` to `=` for historical reasons.
Irene: I captured the outbound requests. curl: `/v1/admin/datasets?filter=name:eq:training` SDK: `/v1/admin/datasets?filter=name=eq%3Atraining` (note `=` used before `eq` and `:` encoded). Backend rejects it as malformed.
Mark: this is a parity regression from codegen change that tried to normalise filter helpers across languages. Go mapping ended up using `field=op:value` style while server kept `field:op:value`.
Luis: workaround: use raw query call `client.Request("GET", "/v1/admin/datasets?filter=name:eq:training")` or pass the full query string via options.
Irene: raw request fixed onboarding. Repro steps added to the ticket.
sdk-bot: Created issue #4019 - "go-sdk: filter helper uses wrong operator separator for admin.datasets (colon vs equals)" and attached HAR + reproduction.
QA-bot: Adding regression test to nightly that runs sampleapp dataset listing with filter variants.
Mark: Proposed fixes: (1) update Go SDK filter helper to emit colon-separated operator syntax, (2) add language-conformance tests for query encoding, (3) add a small golden-URL test to CI for admin dataset/list.
Luis: Also audit other helper functions that build query strings (sorting, facets)  they share the same codepath.
Irene: thanks all  workaround in place; will retry onboarding once patch lands. :+1:
